Tree

A file tree or an outline whose folders open and close with no script, built on nested details elements.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For the files of a repository, a worktree or a change set, where the reader opens a folder to find a file.
  • For the outline of a long document or a plan, with sections that hold links to their parts.
  • Beside the content it navigates, in a sidebar or the list region of a split panel.

When not to use it

  • For items with no hierarchy. Use a list.
  • For the destinations of the app. Use the sidebar nav.
  • For one piece of detail that opens in place. Use a disclosure.
  • For a hierarchy deeper than two levels of folders. Write the rest of the path into the folder's name, such as src/auth/providers, or open the deep folder as a view of its own.
  • Where items must be selected, dragged or renamed in place with the arrow keys. That is an ARIA tree, which this is not: build it as an app-local component.

Variants

file tree
The default. Each folder's summary holds a folder icon and each file a file icon, both with gw-tree__icon.
outline
The same markup without the icons, for the sections of a document or a plan.

Sizes

default
Every row is at least 44px tall. Each level is set in 20px behind a rule.

Accessibility

  • Use a nav with the class gw-tree and an aria-label that says what the tree holds, or a div where the tree does not navigate. Inside it, a ul with gw-tree__list and one li per row.
  • A folder is a details element with gw-tree__branch. Its summary, with gw-tree__summary, holds an optional icon, the name in a span with gw-tree__name, and optionally a fact in words in a span with gw-tree__meta, such as 3 changed files. After the summary comes a nested ul with gw-tree__list.
  • A file or an outline entry is an a element with gw-tree__leaf, or a button with type="button" where it selects without navigating. It holds the same icon, name and optional fact.
  • This is a disclosure tree, not role="tree". The ARIA tree role would oblige the app to script every key, one tab stop, aria-expanded, aria-level, aria-setsize and aria-posinset, and it reads poorly on touch screen readers. Nested details give a screen reader a list with its item count, a button that says collapsed or expanded, and links, with no script at all.
  • Tab moves through the rows that are shown. Enter or Space on a folder opens or closes it, and Enter follows a file's link. There are no arrow-key bindings, and the browser's find-in-page opens a closed folder that holds a match.
  • Folders nest at most two levels, the system's limit for disclosures. The checker reports a third as disclosure-depth. Fold a longer path into one folder's name.
  • Mark the item in view with aria-current on its leaf: "page" for a file that has its own view, "location" for a place in the document, "true" otherwise. It is drawn with a bar and a heavier name as well as a shade. Open the folders that hold it with the open attribute.
  • Icons are decoration and carry aria-hidden="true". A change is written in words, such as 38 added, 12 removed, never as a colour.
  • For a folder that is empty, loading or unreadable, put one li with gw-tree__note in its list: a sentence, a spinner with its text, or a sentence with role="alert" and a button that loads again.
  • To load a folder's rows when it first opens, the app listens for the details element's toggle event. Nothing else needs script.
